utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I ask the Registrar to call out the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-PT, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, Vladimir Santic, also known as Vlado.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: May I have the appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Terree Bowers for the Prosecution, with my colleague, Michael Blaxill. We also have the case analyst, Bill Smith, and the case manager, Adele Erasmus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could I have the appearances for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I am Ranko Radovic from Croatia for Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MRS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am attorney Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac from Zagreb appearing on behalf of Mr Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am attorney Borislav Krajina from Sarajevo appearing on behalf of Vlatko Kupreskic, together with colleague Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, my name is Zelimir Par. I am from Zagreb and appearing on behalf of the accused, Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I am Luka Susak from Zagreb appearing on behalf of Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am attorney Petar Puliselic from Zagreb appearing on behalf of Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour, and Mr President. I am Petar Pavkovic, attorney from Zagreb, the Republic of Croatia, appearing on behalf of Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We feel that we are now confronted with five different issues which we should deal with today. You cannot hear me? Can all the defendants hear me in Croatian? Can you hear me now -- all of you? Thank you. I will say that we are confronted with five different issues which we would like and we hope to be able to deal with today. First of all, the Prosecution's motion for leave to amend the indictment. The second item is the Defence counsel request for assignment of counsel having no command of either English or French. The third item is the request by Vlatko Kupreskic for returning items from his briefcase. Then we have the question of the Defence motion on the form of the indictment and, lastly, we should be able to hold the status conference. May I propose that, first of all, we deal with the Prosecutor's motion for leave to amend the indictment, and before we hear argument, I would like to say that we, the court, accepts the Prosecutor's reply filed on 5 March 1998. I would like now to ask the Prosecutor to present their argument on this motion. I wonder whether you could confine yourself to, say, 10 or 15 minutes -- would that be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: I think it can be shorter than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Wonderful. Then I will turn to the Defence counsel and I wonder whether each of them could address this issue for, say, five to 10 minutes. After that, we will try to make a ruling on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. As we have set forth in our reply, there are really only three fundamental changes to the amended indictment. The first one is the omission of the Article 2 offences, and that is really in the interests of expediting the trial. It does not really change the underlying criminal conduct. By eliminating the Article 2 charges, we are able to forgo introduction of the evidence concerning international armed conflict, which we think should result in a substantial savings in time for the trial itself. So that is the first fundamental change. The second fundamental change involves the dropping of the charges against Dragan Papic in relation to the trench digging activities and the killing incident out at the trenches. On further investigation, the attorneys who will be actually prosecuting this case do not feel that those counts are viable and, therefore, they have been withdrawn. For the purposes of the trial, Dragan Papic is now included in the persecution count as opposed to the original charges involving the trench digging and the trench digging killing incident. The other fundamental change involves the elimination of the unlawful attack charge, which is a more technical offence pertaining to the military execution of an actual attack, and we have substituted the persecution charge in its place. Any of the other changes are simply minor wording changes which do not in any way change the underlying fact patterns. I think the core of the case is the same -- there has been substantial testimony in the Blaskic case regarding the attack on Ahmici. I think all of the Defence is aware of the alleged underlying criminal activity and I think there is sufficient notice with regard to the individual participants and their role in the attack. We would simply submit that the supporting material which we have presented to the court is more than sufficient to meet the very threshold inquiry which the court is charged with today, and that is to demonstrate that there are reasonable grounds for believing that there was criminal conduct within the jurisdiction of the Tribunal. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now turn to the Defence and I would like to ask Defence counsel to follow the order in which the accused are listed on the indictment. So, first of all, therefore the Defence counsel for Zoran Kupreskic and, as I say, I would like to make an appeal and ask Defence counsel whether each of them could confine himself or herself to about five to 10 minutes, to just this particular point. Counsel for Zoran Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, regarding what has been stated by the Prosecutor, the Defence accepts only the point made regarding the dropping of the international conflict and we agree with that amendment to the indictment. As regards the other element, we have to draw the attention of the court to the fact that this indictment was issued in 1995, that it was confirmed by the Tribunal, and that only immediately before the beginning of trial, on the basis of the same grounds that were used for the original indictment, he is proposing an amendment. We therefore feel that the Prosecutor has no new evidence which would justify the other changes to the indictment. In addition, we wish to draw the attention of the court to the fact that, in the individual charges, the Prosecutor is describing legally the act and not indicating the actual facts which come under the individual Articles of the Statute. For example, in count 9 and 10, reference is made to this group of the accused, saying that they participated in military training, armament, the evacuation of Bosnian Croats and preparation of homes for attacks. Then, also, there is reference made to groups of soldiers going from one house to another attacking civilians and their property, without making any mention at all of the role of the actual accused and what their specific acts were. In further specifying the charges in count 1, persecution, the time period is extended and all the accused are charged for the period from October 1992. Though, as I have said, there are absolutely no new facts or evidence which would give the Prosecutor the possibility to expand the time period for which the criminal charges are being made. The Defence of the accused -- we recognise there is the statement of Sakib Ahmic and we cannot go into the authenticity or credibility of his statement or, rather, whether his statement can serve for condemnation of the accused, so we will leave that for a subsequent period of the trial. Therefore, our final proposal would be to retain the time period that you have given us and, to do that, we would agree to adopting only that amendment regarding the dropping of the point regarding international conflict, whereas all the other amendments should not be accepted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MRS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr Radovic and I are together defending Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic -- the first and second accused, so as to avoid any confusion -- and I agree with everything that my learned colleague has said, because it applies to both the defendants. I should also like to point out -- I do not know whether it is an error, or a major mistake by the Prosecution -- but I must say, first, that I also agree that the international conflict should be left out, and, in this way, we can expedite the proceedings, which is our common aim and, also, we agree with the changes in the qualifications. However, in point 24 of the amended indictment, a description of the act, it is stated that Zoran Kupreskic, armed with an automatic weapon, entered the Ahmic house and shot and killed Naser Ahmic. In count 2, in the legal description, it is stated that Zoran Kupreskic and Mirjan Kupreskic thereby committed a crime against humanity and violated the laws or customs of war. Therefore, there is no incrimination for Mirjan Kupreskic in the counts. In item 25 it is stated that Mirjan Kupreskic entered the house later on, so I see no reason why, in the actual incriminations, Mirjan Kupreskic should be charged with two criminal offences, whereas, in the description, no mention is made, and this is quite unusual. Furthermore, in the original indictment, Mirjan Kupreskic was not charged with the murder of Naser Ahmic. I do not know how this came about. Furthermore, according to the statement of Sakib Ahmic, I do not think that the court should evaluate the evidence, but, as supporting material, this statement of Sakib Ahmic is such that he says that Mirjan Kupreskic was not armed, or rather, he said that he did not see Mirjan Kupreskic wearing arms. After that, Mirjan Kupreskic is charged with four murder offences. Therefore, I think that either the Prosecution has not been specific enough in describing the case -- the charges -- or he has additional evidence that we have not seen, and which serves as a basis for these charges. So, I should like the Prosecution to comment on these points, because this is not clear to us, and we consider this to be a major error on the part of the Prosecution. Another point I should like to make that has to do with point 9 of the background -- it actually describes acts of which not one is a criminal offence. For instance, reference is made to "evacuation", "failure to inform neighbours", "arming under war conditions" -- these are not criminal offences. Regardless of that, this is used to charge the accused with crimes against humanity, under Article 5(a). I think that this point should be omitted, as it lacks precision and foundation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Your Honour. Contrary to our response to the proposal of the Prosecution to amend the indictment, we propose that this motion be rejected and we wish to point out that Vlatko Kupreskic, and we as their Defence, have still not availed ourselves of the right to submit motions regarding the original indictment, because we were given notice that it would be amended. We are therefore in a slightly less favourable position than the other Defence counsel, who have already had occasion to voice their opinion regarding the original indictment. The deadline for motions for Vlatko Kupreskic expires on 16 March this year, and we still do not know when a ruling will be made regarding the request of the Prosecution to amend the indictment. Therefore, we may find ourselves in a situation where, in the event that the request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment is rejected, in that case our time limit may run out for submitting motions. Therefore, we appeal to the Trial Chamber that, in the event of the request of the Prosecution being rejected, we are given another eight days for submitting motions regarding the original indictment. As for the response to the request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment, which we have submitted to the Trial Chamber, and after hearing the response of the Prosecution to our reply, we still abide by the original proposal that this request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment be rejected. The main thesis of the Defence counsel of Vlatko Kupreskic, which we argued in our response, is that the evidence which our learned friend, the Prosecution, presented, in our view, is not sufficient to confirm the indictment. Of course, this will be determined by the Trial Chamber, but allow me to make only a few points. The accused, Vlatko Kupreskic, is, as we see, facing the supreme penal Tribunal, charged with very grave crimes -- war crimes -- and violations of the laws and customs of war. Such serious accusations, in our view, require a certain standard of evidence, which must be understandable to all legal systems. However, in support of this indictment, we do not see the Prosecution offering that kind of evidence, namely, with respect to point 1 of the amended indictment, which has to do with the persecution of Muslims on religious and political grounds, where the incrimination is intentional killing of Bosnian Muslims, systematic destruction of homes and property of Bosnian Muslims, the organisation, detention and expulsion of Muslims from Ahmici, Santici, et cetera, there is not a single element of proof to confirm such charges. Out of the three statements offered by the Prosecution, not a single one contains a relevant fact which could be linked to what the accused, Vlatko Kupreskic, is charged with. Contrary to this, the Defence, in support of its reply regarding the request for amending the indictment, has offered statements by Muslims and other factual evidence, which, in our opinion, indisputably show that Vlatko Kupreskic, at the relevant time period, was not a participant in political or military life, that he had no authorisations or powers of that kind, and therefore could not, in the way described in the indictment, have planned the attack on Ahmici, nor could he have organised the systematic persecution of Muslims. If necessary, the Defence can, in more detail, analyse those witness statements and other evidence offered by the Prosecution in support of this count. We therefore feel that, with respect to count 1, there is no relevant evidence that could incriminate the accused, Vlatko Kupreskic. Regarding the crime against humanity and breaches of the customs and laws of war from counts 12 to 15 of the indictment, having to do with the killing of Fata Pezer and the wounding of Dzenana Pezer. A brief reference to these charges will be made by my colleague, Zelimir Par. That is the agreement we have reached between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, points 12 to 15 of the amended indictment deal with a specific event which took place on 16 April 1993, when Vlatko Kupreskic is accused with the murder of one person and the wounding of another. Regardless of the fact that the legal description of these acts is "crimes against humanity" and "violations of the laws and customs of war", we feel that the substance of this act is murder and bodily injury -- in this case, with firearms. Therefore, the evidence confirming the accusations of this kind, we feel, need to contain all elements that would prove the cause of death and the instrument used for committing the act, the way in which the act was committed, the time when it was committed, the place when it was committed, and the perpetrator of the act. In this specific case, the Prosecutor has, in support of these charges, submitted only one evidence; that is, a statement of an unnamed witness, whose identity was subsequently disclosed. The Defence has analysed the statement of this witness and considers the statement to be contrary to the allegations contained in both indictments. With respect to the first indictment, we feel that the statement of the witness is untruthful, because the place where the witness was at the time -- in view of the place where he was, he was not in a position to see the accused, Vlatko Kupreskic, nor where Vlatko Kupreskic allegedly was at the time according to the indictment. The Defence bases this view on a video recording, which we made on the spot, regarding the place of the act, the place where they were wounded, the position where the witness was at the time, and how this position relates to the yard of Vlatko Kupreskic's house, or rather the spot where allegedly this witness saw Vlatko Kupreskic. Therefore, we submit, on the basis of this videotape, that there was no possibility of the witness seeing the event from the position where he allegedly stood. We will ask the Trial Chamber to allow us to show this videotape as evidence. By making this videotape, we followed the allegations of the Prosecution and we submit that that statement is untruthful, because the witness was not objectively able to see what he claims he saw. Regarding the amended indictment, points 12 to 15, it differs from the original one insofar as the factual events have been described differently. In doing so, the Prosecution has indicated the direction of movement of the victims by saying that they were moving by Vlatko Kupreskic's house, whereas earlier, in the original indictment, it said they were moving towards the woods. This change is of first rate importance to the Defence, because we feel that whether the accused Vlatko Kupreskic could have perpetrated these acts depends very much on the locations and, therefore, this change of location now places Vlatko Kupreskic in a position when he has to defend himself quite differently from the original indictment. In his submission of 5 March, the Prosecution has responded to this objection, saying that the description has been made more specific, but that thereby the direction of movement has not been changed. The Prosecution alleges that this was essential for the indictment so as to place the victims in the line of fire -- the Defence and the Prosecution, with respect to this particular point, that is, whether a change of direction of movement has been changed or not, we differ, because we continue to claim that the place has been changed as a result and that the statement of the only witness offered by the Prosecution does not show that they were passing by the house, nor has the Prosecution offered any new evidence to confirm that allegation. The Prosecutor probably knows that there are two roads leading up to upper Ahmici. One passes by the house of Vlatko Kupreskic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder if you could confine yourself to matters to be dealt with at this stage? You are raising matters which are to be discussed at trial, so please do not go into questions of evidence, facts and so on. You know that for the confirmation of the -- non-confirmation of the amendment to the indictment, only a prima facie case is required, so, please, therefore, confine yourself to dealing with these particular matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I shall try and be more concise. It is my opinion that we are talking about the proposal to amend the indictment under points 12 to 15. The Prosecutor has made certain changes which we feel it has not substantiated, and I am trying to show why the change in the description is essential and why the Defence requests that this be rejected, because we feel that the event has been changed -- the description of the event has been changed without being corroborated by additional evidence, and that is why I have spoken at maybe greater length, because the Defence would like this point to be cleared up. Also, the position of the Defence is such that we feel that our defendant, Vlatko Kupreskic, who is now in custody, who is physically of impaired health and who is asking this Trial Chamber that the evidence submitted against him should be dealt with as soon as possible, because, for him, it is very important how long the proceedings will last in view of his physical condition and, for him, detention has highly unfavourable consequences. I will conclude my statement by saying that, for these reasons, we will submit a motion for the release of Vlatko Kupreskic and I feel that, in the specific case, which can be seen from an analysis of these points, that the charges against him have been made only because the army was in his house and that it was from his house that some shots were fired and that is why the indictment is being linked to Vlatko Kupreskic. Therefore, the Defence of Vlatko Kupreskic proposes to the Trial Chamber that the request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment be rejected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Vladimir Santic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr President, your Honours, there are three points which I shall try, within the time limit allotted to us, to raise. In the first place, the Defence counsel is grateful to the Trial Chamber for giving us this opportunity to review issues regarding the form of the indictment -- in spite of the position of the Prosecution referring to Article 47. It is my opinion that the Prosecutor is formally right when it considers it to be its exclusive right to shape the indictment, but I would like to remind the Prosecutor that, for him, as for all of us participants in the trial, the Rules oblige us to carry out an expeditious trial and the right you have given us is a right which goes in line with this idea of a speedy and efficient trial and that is why I consider your decision to be quite in order and acceptable. That is one point I wanted to make. A second point: with respect to the request of the Prosecution to amend the indictment dated 9 February this year, the Defence has already, in its written submission, presented its views regarding this request for amending the indictment, and, respecting the time limit, I do not wish to repeat what we said then. I just wish to draw attention to the following: on page 4 of our response, in sentence 2, a printing error has been made, so although the meaning of the text is clear, will you please take note of this? It says there, "Are also based on" and what should be written is "are also not based on". This corresponds to the substance of the text that precedes this paragraph. What is it I wish to point out? We heard the Prosecutor -- that the material submitted in support of amending the indictment refers to evidence in support of the conviction that my defendant also committed the crimes that the Prosecutor has charged him with. One does not have to be a legal expert. It is sufficient to read the witness statement, which the Prosecutor intends to offer to the court in order to support their allegations to come to the conclusion that what he says is simply a speculation. Not one of the witnesses offered by the Prosecution has confirmed that my defendant, my client, has committed the crimes described in the amended indictment under paragraphs 9, 10, 20 and 21. When talking about the alleged crimes committed by my client as described in paragraphs 16 to 19, again, the allegation of the Prosecution cannot be confirmed. There is only a single witness who speaks about my client. I accept, Mr President, your remark and I will not analyse the statement of that witness. However, I must draw attention to the fact, because the Prosecutor responded on 5 February to our reply, by saying that these are accusations contained in the request which are substantive to the indictment and which this court has confirmed -- that is the original indictment. I should just like to remind the Prosecutor that in the meantime certain qualitative changes have taken place, which seriously call in question the statement of this witness. My third point, and one that I wish to underline in particular: in the country I come from, and which relies on the European legal tradition, and in my own modest knowledge of the legal system of the Prosecutor, I have not found evidence of the Prosecution threatening with accusations, as he has done in his brief in support of the request for amending the indictment. The Prosecutor does not announce future incriminations whereby he is already affecting -- further affecting the already impaired health of my client. The materials submitted are dated 5 February this year, so these are very fresh knowledge that he has, only four days preceding the compiling of this request, and he says that he will be submitting additional indictments, but on the basis of what material and how long should we wait for these new indictments to be issued? I submit that the request of the Prosecutor for amending the indictment be rejected, because my client has not committed a single crime mentioned in this request. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I pass on to the next legal counsel, may I apologise for reading from a wrong list of indictees and therefore Defence counsel. It actually properly would be Josipovic after Kupreskic and then Papic and Santic. I apologise, this was a wrong list. My second point is you know there is no legal system to be applied by the Prosecutor as distinct from the legal system which must be applied by the Defence and the Tribunal. There is only one legal system, which is a body of law, which we have to apply here in this International Criminal Tribunal, and it is based on our Statute, our Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the general principle of -- principles of criminal law as adopted in all major legal systems. I now call upon the legal counsel for Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr President, your Honours, I would like to abide by my response made as the Defence counsel in response to the request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment. In paragraphs 9, 10, 20 and 21 of the amended indictment, in my view, there is no proof -- no evidence that Drago Josipovic committed the acts he is charged with. There is not a single witness statement that would accuse him of those crimes. However, I wanted to say something else, since the previous speakers have already commented on this, especially colleagues Radovic and Pavkovic. I will be very brief in my comments with regard to these amendments. In the first place, I think there is no individual description of any one of these criminal offences. Then, the actual place or time of the act has not been indicated. I think these are generalisations and there is no specification of the circumstances which would describe the actual criminal offence with which Drago Josipovic is charged. As regards paragraph 20 of the amended indictment, it is my view that the Prosecutor is familiar with the statement of witness Fatima Ahmic, because they have already referred to evidence submitted in the Blaskic case, and it emerges from that that Drago Josipovic had a positive attitude towards the Muslims. Therefore, I consider that this paragraph is unfounded, because, in addition to what I have said, there is no other witness statement that would show that this crime was committed by Drago Josipovic. As for paragraph 21, it is confusing and vague, because it follows from it that Drago Josipovic committed and aided and abetted in a particular crime, so two forms of a commission of an act cannot be attributed to a single perpetrator. The more so, as here the legal descriptions are given rather than the description of the actual act. Therefore, I propose that the request be rejected, except that we do support the dropping of the reference to an international conflict. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Dragan Papic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours. The accused, Dragan Papic, and I as his Defence counsel, find ourselves in a slightly different position than the majority of the other accused and their Defence counsels with respect to the amended indictment, because the amended indictment which this Trial Chamber is going to rule on, that is to accept it or reject it, my client, my defendant, Dragan Papic, it seems to me is being charged with a smaller quantity -- a smaller amount of criminal activity than in the indictment from 1995. Namely, according to that original indictment, Dragan Papic was charged with a number of offences coming under Articles 2 and 3 of the Statute, whereas now he is charged under Article 5(h) only of the Tribunal's Statute. Perhaps it may therefore, at first glance, appear strange that I, as Defence counsel, am not supportive of this amended indictment, because, even though it is more favourable for my client, Dragan Papic, especially with respect to the one from 1995, and in my brief, in response to the Prosecutor's request, I have proposed that it be rejected. This does not mean to say that I support or accept the 1995 indictment, but I will not go into that today, as that is not the subject of this hearing. I should just like to refer, with a couple of sentences, to the reasons why the Defence finds that the amended indictment is not acceptable with regard to Dragan Papic. In paragraph 20, it is stated that Dragan Papic persecuted the Bosnian Muslim inhabitants of Ahmici, Santici, on political, religious and racial grounds, by planning and organising an attack, which was designed to remove all Bosnian Muslims from the area. However, from the material that has been disclosed to the Defence, accompanying the amended indictment, and which should provide factual support in favour of the indictment, it does not emerge that Dragan Papic had planned or organised the ethnic cleansing of Bosnian Muslims. In these materials, there is not a word to that effect. Finally, Dragan Papic, as an ordinary private, an ordinary soldier with an insignificant role could not have planned and organised such activities, even if he had wanted to -- the activities which are allegedly described as ethnic cleansing of Bosnian Muslims. Furthermore, the supporting materials for the amended indictment do not point to evidence of Dragan Papic participating in the systematic killing of Bosnian Muslims, as is stated in paragraph 21(a) of the indictment. Also, there is nothing in the material to show that Dragan Papic destroyed Bosnian Muslim homes and property, as is alleged in paragraph 21(b) of the amended indictment. Furthermore, not a single witness mentioned in the supporting materials, and several of them mention Dragan Papic, not one of them confirms the allegation of the indictment that Dragan Papic had in any way participated in organising the detention and expulsion of Bosnian Muslims from Ahmici and Santici as stated in paragraph 21(c) of the indictment. Paragraph 22 of the amended indictment, amongst other things, refers to paragraph 9, but from the supporting material provided with the indictment, it does not follow that Papic Dragan had indeed participated in military training and arming or in the evacuation of Bosnian Muslims on the night before the attack, in organising the HVO soldiers, in preparing his house and the house of his relatives for operations, or in preparing other locations to be used for attack. All these alleged activities of Dragan Papic referred to have been qualified by the Prosecution as a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Tribunal's Statute; that is, as persecution on political, racial or religious grounds. Not a single part of the amended indictment shows in what way Dragan Papic had specifically participated in any one of these acts that are attributed to him. One cannot see how he planned or organised the persecution of Bosnian Muslims; one cannot see how he had systematically killed Bosnian Muslims, when the indictment does not mention any individual who whom he had allegedly killed. So, the Defence does not understand what there is to show that Dragan Papic participated in the demolition of Bosnian Muslim homes and their property. If there is no indication how he did that, whose houses and property he destroyed, and if the supporting material does not make any reference to these specific acts, therefore, in the opinion of the Defence, the supporting material disclosed to the Defence in support of the amended indictment does not provide the Prosecutor with any argument to charge Dragan Papic under Article 5(h) of the Statute that is for the persecution of Bosnian Muslims on political, racial or religious grounds. That is why the Defence proposes, as it has done in its written brief, that the request of the Prosecution for amending the indictment be rejected, because there is no prima facie case in favour of such an amendment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I would like to ask now the Prosecutor whether there is any -- it would like to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we have a few comments. With regard to the persecution count itself, what the Prosecution will show at trial is that the attack on Ahmici had as its primary purpose the ethnic cleansing of the Muslim population. By virtue of that attack where a significant portion of the civilian population was killed, and Muslim homes were burnt to the ground, Muslim livestock was slaughtered and the entire Muslim population was deported out of the village, our position is that there is strong circumstantial evidence that this was coordinated and planned. Our position with regard to the individual defendants is that they were all, Article 7(1), aiders and abettors to this overall strategy and our submission would be that there is more than adequate circumstantial evidence from the supporting material given to the court to meet the threshold Rule 47 standard with regard to these allegations. With regard to Mirjan Kupreskic specifically, there is no mistake in the indictment. That is absolutely an intentional charging decision. Our position there is that Mirjan and Zoran approached the Ahmic home with the intention of killing all the inhabitants and burning the home to the ground. That is precisely what they did. They are aiders and abettors of each other and Mirjan would not have had to pull the trigger on any weapon to be guilty of the murder as an aider and abettor. That is our theory and again we think we have more than sufficient evidence to meet the Rule 47 threshold standard. With regard to Vlatko Kupreskic and the sightings, as the court correctly noted, most of the arguments that the Defence offered regarding the sightings of Vlatko Kupreskic's house and the shooting coming from that house, most of those arguments have to do with evidence at trial. I would just reiterate we have not changed the route of escape. We simply wanted to make it clear that our position is that there was firing coming from the area of Vlatko Kupreskic's home, and it was that firing that ended up killing the one individual and wounding the other. With regard to Dragan Papic, we would point out that there has been extensive new evidence presented in the single declaration with regard to his participation. It is important to note that, in the attack of October 20th, there is an allegation that he is the only person that killed someone in that initial attack on Ahmici. Our position will be that that October attack started the events that led to the eventual planning and coordination of the final attack on Ahmici which ethnically cleansed it. It is important to note that the allegation is that Dragan Papic was a sniper at that time and actually killed someone. It goes to his expertise, his training. We have allegations that he was a member of the HVO, wore a black and camouflage uniform, had a sniper rifle, and that after October 1992, he actually forced Muslim males to report to the HVO on a daily basis. That also is in the supplementary supporting material. He was seen in possession of automatic weaponry. On the morning of the attack, there was actually sniper fire seen originating from the window of his father's home, where he lived. There were numerous soldiers with camouflage and black uniforms running around his particular house. There was a large machine-gun in front of his house, which indicates prior preparation, and then we have the actual sightings of him on the morning of the actual attack, where he is seen in a doorway in front of a body. He is seen with numerous soldiers, appearing to lead them at different times. That is more than sufficient evidence to show that, again, he is an aider and abettor in this overall persecution charge and, again, he could be found guilty without even pulling the trigger on a weapon, if he is found to be an aider and abettor. We are prepared to address any other specific comments that the court may entertain. We would just point out that we have a great concern here, in that I think that, to a certain extent, this hearing has been misused by the Defence, when it singles out individual witnesses and identifies them by name and attacks their credibility. Many of these witnesses are in very precarious situations, subjected to continuing harassment and intimidation, and it is just inappropriate for this threshold inquiry to involve these sorts of credibility attacks, which only have a role in the trial itself. As the court knows, there are instances when we present supporting material with witnesses for the confirmation of the indictment. When we actually proceed to trial, those individuals may not even testify. So, if the court has any enquiries with regard to the specifics of particular witnesses, we would definitely request that that be in camera. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we adjourn in about half an hour and make our ruling on this matter, I think we should deal with other matters -- some of the other matters that I indicated at the outset of our hearing. First of all, the Defence counsel request for assignment of counsel. Now, we have noted that various requests were filed on 10 and 17 February 1998 by each of the accused, save Mirjan Kupreskic, requesting the assignment to them of counsel who do not speak one of the two working languages of the International Criminal Tribunal, namely English or French. The court has decided to authorise the Registrar to assign to each of the accused, counsel of their choice -- to each of the accused, counsel of their choice, even if that counsel does not speak either of the two working languages of the International Criminal Tribunal, provided, however, that should the accused later seek the assignment of co-counsel, such co-counsel must speak one of the two working languages of the International Tribunal. This is our ruling. As for the question of request by Vlatko Kupreskic, this issue will be dealt with later on in our status conference. I will move on to a third issue -- one of the five issues I mentioned this morning, namely, the Defence motion on the form of indictment. In this respect, I would like to ask Defence counsel if they wish to continue with this motion. Actually, there were four motions. I wonder whether they need to be amended, or whether Defence counsel intend to go ahead with these motions? I wonder whether Defence counsel are prepared to take a stand on this issue, or whether we should put it off until after the status conference. Is there any position by Defence counsel on these four motions on the form of indictment? I think probably you would like to discuss this issue after our ruling on whether or not we grant the motion of the Prosecutor on the amendment of the indictment. Alright, let us put it off until we resume. (Pause). The court is now in a position to make a ruling on the Prosecutor's motion for leave to amend the indictment. The court has decided to grant this motion and we will issue an order to this effect where we set out the reasons for our decision. That means that the accused will have to plead guilty or not guilty to the new charge of persecution. I wonder whether the Defence counsel are prepared to propose a time for the guilty or not guilty plea? You will need some time to consult with your clients and, also, I understand you have not yet been given the text of the revised amendment in Serbo-Croatian -- is that correct? I issued instructions this morning to the effect that a translation into Croatian should be prepared by 12 o'clock at the latest. (Pause). To my regret, I have been told that the translators will not be in a position to provide the Croatian translation of this document before tomorrow afternoon. So let us now have a coffee break so we will adjourn for 20 minutes and then maybe, when we come back --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have very often encountered the problem of translation. We expected that something like this would happen and we have managed to translate the amended indictment and our clients have been advised of the contents of the amended indictment, which further means that they are ready, today, for the purpose of expediting the trial -- they are ready to enter a plea? MR V KUPRESKIC: Your Honour, I would kindly ask you to let me address the court in just a few words, please. I will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: What particular topic -- on what particular subject?. MR V KUPRESKIC: Well, I would like to say something about everything that has been said today. I would just like to say a few words about that. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Alright, I grant you leave to address the court. MR V KUPRESKIC: First of all, let me thank this honourable Chamber for having enabled me to speak. I would also like to thank you for having assigned counsel to me and, furthermore, just because of these situations, this particular case, as my case, my Defence counsel have offered very good evidence, very precise evidence, as have other Defence counsel. We have, therefore, enabled us to be heard today and I would like to say thank you on behalf of my colleagues here, to all of you. I would kindly ask you, as human beings, and then as judges -- I would appeal to your understanding of my situation. I am 100 per cent innocent and I am certain that, because of my health, I will not be able to wait until your decision -- until your finding of not guilty, because it may take a few months or maybe even a year. We have very strong evidence -- we even have a strong alibi of the witness that has been proffered by the Prosecution, of a Muslim woman, by the name of Morisa Strmonja. Therefore, with full responsibility, let me state here before you that you have a witness here -- a witness to the Dayton Accords -- which I can prove with numerous proofs, a lot of evidence and I have also witness statements by Muslims that can prove that. My life and my conduct is all a result or consequence of the Dayton Accords. I do not think that you will allow that agreement -- and I hope we are all in favour of that agreement -- you will not allow this agreement to be tried here before the court. Therefore, let me kindly ask you once again, let me appeal to you not to let -- not to be tried -- not to enter this trial without necessity. I will therefore ask you to consider, as quickly as possible, all the evidence and try to conclude my case as soon as possible, perhaps even today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I am afraid we are not in a position to do so, because we cannot start the trial -- there are pre-trial proceedings which we have to go through. But we are fully sympathetic to your request for an expeditious trial. I can assure you that the trial will start as soon as possible. It is in the interests of justice and in the interests of your right to be tried as quickly as possible. I understand from Defence counsel that all Defence counsel would be ready to move on to their next stage where all the defendants will be asked to plead guilty or not guilty to the new charge. Are you prepared to do so even, say, in half an hour, after we take a recess, so that we can move on to that particular phase? And then we would have the status conference to organise the next steps to be taken before trial commences. Would you be prepared to do so after, say, half an hour -- at quarter to 12 -- when we resume our hearing? Yes? The Prosecutor has no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We stand adjourned for half an hour until quarter to 12. (11.15am) (A short break) (11.50am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I apologise for the five-minute delay and we may now move on to the next issue, namely, the entry of a plea by the various defendants. I understand that all the Defence counsel had an opportunity to talk to their clients and to translate into Croatian the relevant parts of the indictment. However, since we are very keen on the rights of the accused and we think that the rights of the accused must be fully respected, we have decided to ask the Registrar to read out, slowly, the relevant parts of the amended indictment so that all the defendants will be able to follow in Croatian -- the Croatian translation. After that, I will ask all the various defendants --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, our clients are familiar with the entire indictment and not just the relevant parts. They are now prepared to waive their right to have the indictment read to them in its entirety and are ready to proceed to the plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I take it that all the defendants are fully aware of the indictment and I also understand that they had adequate time to confer with their Defence counsel before the initial appearance. Now, I will ask now each defendant to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty, and I would like to ask them to use the following form -- to say either "I plead guilty" when I read out a count, or "I plead not guilty". Let me start with Mr Zoran Kupreskic. Could you please rise and state your name and date of birth? MR Z KUPRESKIC: Your Honours, I am Zoran Kupreskic. I was born 23 September 1958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I will read out count 1 of the amended indictment: A crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) (persecution on political, racial or religious grounds) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? MR Z KUPRESKIC: Your Honours, I am not guilty according to the previous indictment, I am not guilty according to this indictment, and I am not guilty even if there would be 100 million new indictments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 2: A crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) (murder) of the Statute of the Tribunal. MR Z KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 4: crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) (murder) of the Statute of the Tribunal. MR Z KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 6: crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) (murder) of the Statute of the Tribunal. MR Z KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 8: crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) (murder) of the Statute of the Tribunal. MR Z KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 10: a crime against humanity punishable by Article 5(i) (inhumane acts) of the Statute of the Tribunal. MR Z KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Mirjan Kupreskic. MR M KUPRESKIC: Your Honours, I am Mirjan Kupreskic, born 21 October 1963.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 1: Crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal (persecution on political, racial or religious grounds). MR M KUPRESKIC: Your Honours, absolutely not guilty for anything that I am charged with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 2: crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal (murder). MR M KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 4: crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal (murder). MR M KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Vlatko Kupreskic. MR V KUPRESKIC: I am Vlatko Kupreskic, born 1 January 1958. I have a high education and from my birth I have been 100 per cent handicapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 1: Crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal (persecution on political, racial or religious grounds). MR V KUPRESKIC: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 12: crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal (murder). MR V KUPRESKIC: Of course, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You can sit. Mr Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am Dragan Papic, born 15 July 1967 in Santici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now in a position to proceed to our status conference. (12.05pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any requests before we move to the status conference, which will take place in camera? Are there any requests from the Defence counsel or from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, no requests from the Prosecutor. (12.10pm)
